notes: Labels computed on truncated history match the full history at all 64 cut points, and a label is withheld until its own bar has closed. Three deliberate lookaheads were introduced to confirm the tests actually fail. The detector flipped to BEAR on 2025-12-21, eleven days before the forward window, and held BEAR through 100% of 2026 while the composite fell 40.6%.
statement: A market-wide regime detector built from a basket can be causal by construction and still call the 2026 bear early.

notes: Kotegawa's 25-day deviation-rate rebound is a strong idea in a market with mean reversion. Inside a confirmed crypto bear it buys falling knives: the deviation keeps deviating. Kept as the SIDEWAYS branch, where it belongs.
statement: Kotegawa-style deviation reversion (buy 25-day MA deviation below -25%) makes money inside a confirmed BEAR regime.

notes: Every decile was negative inside bear regimes and the top-minus-bottom spread was -0.13%. There is no long-only relative-strength edge to harvest when the whole cross-section is falling; the winners are survivors, not signals, and they are not identifiable ex ante.
statement: Cross-sectional relative-strength selection finds the assets that rise during a bear market.

notes: Buying weakness inside a bear is dominated by buying strength: the surviving rule requires price above BOTH the 200d and the 50d SMA. Weakness-buying loses in every window tested.
statement: Buying weakness (oversold) beats buying strength inside a bear regime.

notes: Measuring drawdown from the running peak bricked strategies: after a large gain, a normal retrace tripped the deleverage ramp and the run could never re-lever. S00852's last trade was 2021-05-19, then nothing for 4.5 years. Operator's mandate is the correct one: risk is measured against the deposit, with a ratcheting floor that banks a fraction of profit.
statement: Drawdown should be measured against the initial capital with a ratcheting profit floor, not against the running peak.

notes: The BEAR label alone is not enough to act on. Early bear (composite 30-50% below its high) is catastrophic: -32.30% over 30 days at a 9% hit rate. Late bear (70-100% below) is +6.86% at 52%. The bear branch now gates on composite depth and episode age.
statement: Inside a BEAR regime, forward returns depend on how deep the composite already is; the label alone is not actionable.

notes: The operator's intuition -- dying assets show it in volume -- does not survive an era split. 'Volume expanding >1.5x' is +3.74% forward-30d on 2017-2021 and -2.00% on 2022-2025. Opposite signs across eras means the effect is regime-specific noise, not a transferable property of dying assets. Turnover is a liquidity filter here, not a signal.
statement: Volume decay identifies assets that are terminally finished and whose rebounds should never be bought.

notes: Unlike volume, structure transfers: an asset more than 60% below its own 200-day high loses 11.91% over the next 30 days on the holdout, n=10129, and the sign is the same on train. Wired into the bear branch as bear_max_below_high, though it proved largely redundant with the existing above-both-SMAs requirement.
statement: Distance below the asset's own 200-day high excludes assets whose rebounds are not worth buying, and it transfers across eras.

notes: THE MOST IMPORTANT RESULT SO FAR. With the deleverage ramp on, entry period 15 returned +189% and period 12 returned -9%: a 3-bar change moved trades from 413 to 2251. With the ramp OFF, every period from 8 to 30 returns the IDENTICAL -25.51%, 75 trades, 70.14% exposure, ABORTED. The parameter does nothing. The apparent optimum was which side of a path-dependent throttle bifurcation the run landed on. This retroactively invalidates the +4705% pre-2026 winner and makes every parameter sweep in this project suspect until re-run with the ramp disabled.
statement: The bear breakout entry period has an optimum that can be found by sweeping it.

notes: Progression across unseen windows is monotone and negative: +4705% train, +89% holdout, -11% in 2026. Bear days are +4.30% forward-30d in 2017-2021 and -6.68% in 2022-2025 -- the eras are different markets, and the anti-correlation is visible without opening 2026 at all. Selecting harder pre-2026 makes 2026 worse. The champion S00743 at +3.46% stands.
statement: A configuration selected to maximise the pre-2026 holdout will also perform well in 2026.

notes: The entries are not the problem and the regime label is not the problem: 86 of 224 trades in 2026 hit take-profit at +12.62%. The EXIT is the problem. SIGNAL_EXIT closed 128 trades at a 2% win rate for -46,716 in 2026 and 858 trades at 10% for -806,635 on the holdout. The structure is in holding period and it is the same in both eras: everything resolving within 3 days makes money (holdout +902,068 at 85% win, 2026 +19,716 at 66%) and everything held longer loses (holdout -823,664 across the 3d+ buckets, 2026 -30,382). Unlike H-007's volume signal, the sign does NOT flip between 2017-21, 2022-25 and 2026. Caveat carried into H-012: bucketing by realised duration is conditional on outcome, so a hard time stop must be TESTED, not assumed -- cutting at day 3 truncates a loser at its day-3 loss, it does not convert it into a winner. Also fixed a defect in the decomposer itself: it read a non-existent 'exposure' key off the equity curve and reported 0.0% monthly exposure against a 21.22% average.
statement: The 2026 loss has an anatomy we have never looked at; decomposing it will point at the piece that is actually broken.

notes: The mechanism is real pre-2026 and it is not a throttle artifact -- unlike H-009 the effect is identical with the ramp on (+400.10%) and off (+400.15%), it is monotone in the parameter with an interior optimum at 2 days (1d gives +259.90%, so the edge is not at the boundary), exposure is flat at 32-33% across every cell so it is not leverage, and it improves EVERY configuration tried while converting two that previously breached the drawdown mandate into legal ones (cap 0.10 w0.6: -25.51% ABORTED becomes +443.70% legal; participation: +37.30% ABORTED becomes +282.47% legal). A 4.5x holdout improvement produced NOTHING in 2026: control -11.04%, 2d -12.57%, 3d -12.00%, 5d -10.04%. Slightly worse, not better. Trade count in 2026 rose 227 to 657 and the return did not move, which means the extra turnover only paid extra costs -- the 2026 ENTRIES have no edge to recycle capital into. The take-profit share is the tell: 58% of holdout trades reached target versus 38% in 2026. This is H-010's lesson repeating with a far stronger pre-2026 effect, and it is now the second independent demonstration that pre-2026 improvement does not survive the 2026 boundary. The time stop is kept in the code because it dominates on the holdout at no cost and defaults to off; it is NOT the answer to 2026. Next: the honest null nobody has run -- hold cash in BEAR and measure whether the bear module is worth having at all.
statement: A hard maximum holding period fixes the exit defect found in H-011, and the fix transfers to 2026.

notes: Refuted pre-2026 and confirmed for 2026, which is the whole problem in one line. On the 2022-2025 holdout the bear module earns its keep decisively: flat in BEAR returns +134.49% against +400.15% with the bear branch active, so participation is worth 266 points and deleting it would throw away two thirds of the return. Bull-only is -0.30% and ABORTED, so the regime branches are not decoration. But 2026 is labelled BEAR for 100% of the year, so flat-in-bear IS cash there, and cash returns 0.00% against -10.04% for our best bear rule and -20.73% for our worst. Cash beats everything we have built, in 2026 only. Three hypotheses now agree from different directions (H-010 selection, H-012 exits, H-013 the module itself): the 2022-2025 bear produced bounces our rules could catch and the 2026 bear does not. Also worth recording: flat-in-bear without the time stop ABORTS on the ratchet mandate at 10.56% capital drawdown -- sitting in cash during bear does not protect a run that has already banked a floor and then gives it back in the other regimes.
statement: The bear module is not worth having: holding cash in BEAR beats every bear rule we have built.

notes: iteration exceeded 5400s with no record and was reclaimed by tick

Pre-2026 this is the strongest result the project has produced and the only change that ever improved return and risk together: +708.60% against a +89.29% control, with peak drawdown nearly halved from 56.63% to 29.71%. Per-asset routing alone (+416.29%) beats market routing plus the time stop (+400.15%) with no time stop at all. In 2026 it is -19.97% against a -11.04% control -- nine points WORSE, and the worst forward result of any legal configuration tested. The decomposition is the real finding. Every configuration runs 21-23% exposure in 2026 and the reference basket fell 38.06% over the window, so beta alone explains about -8%. Subtracting it: market scope -2.95% alpha, asset scope -11.19%. Pre-2026 optimisation does not merely fail to transfer, it BUYS NEGATIVE ALPHA roughly one for one -- the harder a configuration is selected on the holdout, the more it underperforms its own beta in 2026. Spearman rank correlation between holdout and 2026 return across six configurations is -0.371. This is the third and strongest demonstration after H-010 and H-012, and it indicts the selection criterion rather than any individual mechanism: maximising pre-2026 return is not a neutral proxy for 2026, it is actively anti-predictive. Also recorded and unexplained: opening the bear-phase gate produced a bit-identical +708.60% in asset scope, so that gate never binds once the market label stops choosing the branch. Kept in the code, off by default, because the holdout risk profile is genuinely better and because the 386-asset universe now has a per-asset detector we did not have before.
statement: Routing on the asset's own regime instead of the market's reaches the assets that rise during a market-wide bear, and that reaches 2026.

notes: No criterion tested is predictive, and the sample cannot establish that any would be. Six configurations give a permutation critical value of |rho| >= 0.771 for one-tailed p<0.05; the best criterion scored +0.371 for the regime-matched late-bear sub-period, p=0.329. Every full-holdout criterion is negative or zero: total return -0.371, worst rolling 12m -0.714, return over drawdown -0.371, monthly dispersion -0.029, beta-stripped alpha -0.086. Selecting for STABILITY is the most anti-predictive of all, which was not expected -- asset scope has a worst-12-month of -5.04% against market scope's -47.63% and is nine points worse in 2026. Risk-adjusted return is no better than raw return. Stripping beta from the holdout return carries no information either. The only non-negative sign belongs to the single criterion restricted to a 2026-like window, which is suggestive of the right direction and is nowhere near evidence. The real constraint is now explicit and it is structural: we have ONE forward window and six paired observations, so no selection rule can be learned from this data at any effect size we could plausibly have. Caught a defect in the harness mid-iteration: the first run gave cap0.10 w0.6 a concurrency of 100 while its paired 2026 number came from the configured default of 12, comparing two different strategies and inflating that row from +443.70% to +626.52%. Re-run matched; it moved worst_rolling_12m from -0.600 to -0.714 and late_bear from +0.257 to +0.371, changing no conclusion. Practical consequence: do not switch criteria on this evidence, and stop treating pre-2026 improvement as progress toward 2026. The next hypothesis should be structural -- control exposure directly rather than search for a configuration -- because searching is the activity this iteration showed we cannot validate.
statement: Some pre-2026 statistic other than total return ranks configurations in a way that predicts 2026.

notes: REFUTED AS STATED, and the correction matters more than the hypothesis. The target is comfortably inside the feasible set. On the 227 trades our system actually opened in 2026: actual -11.04%, perfect entry filter +41.15%, exit at the 10% target wherever it was reachable +55.36%, exit at the high +97.04%. 44% of 2026 trades touched the take-profit target at some point and mean MFE is +11.64%, so the average 2026 trade RISES about 11.6% and closes about 1.3% BELOW entry. The entries are not the defect. I had concluded the opposite in an earlier summary and that was wrong. What is more, the excursion structure is era-stable, which almost nothing in this project has been: give-back is +14.25% per trade on the holdout against +12.93% in 2026, mean MFE +15.15% against +11.64%, mean MAE -13.01% against -10.25%. Unlike H-007 volume, H-010 selection and H-014R scope, this shape does not flip and it does not degrade much across the boundary, so a mechanism fitted to it pre-2026 has a defensible reason to transfer. The bounds use perfect foresight by construction and only a fraction is realisable; their job is to say whether the target is reachable at all, and it is. The causal mechanism that attacks give-back without foresight is a TRAILING STOP, which this project has never tested. The time stop was a crude proxy and failed for an unrelated reason -- it recycled capital into entries that had no edge, whereas a trailing stop protects the excursion an entry has already produced and adds no turnover.
statement: The 30-40% target is outside what our entries can produce in 2026, so the entries must be replaced.

REFUTED, and it is the fourth independent observation of the same thing. The search did what it was asked: the winning configuration is positive in all four disjoint folds (+2.1%, +30.1%, +25.2%, +30.7%) at a worst drawdown of 10.0%, and run across the whole fitted era it returns +166.68% at 10.65% drawdown with a 78.3% win rate. Taken once to the sealed window it returns -6.78%. The hand-set defaults returned 0.00% in the same window by standing aside, so FITTING MADE 2026 WORSE -- consistent with the recorded anti-predictivity of pre-2026 selection (Spearman -0.371). The mechanism is visible in the genome rather than mysterious: it settled on take_profit 4% against stop_loss 44%, a shape that compounds many small wins while the rare loser is eleven times the winner. That survives an era where advances persist and does not survive 2026, where the median asset fell 47% -- 59.4% of forward trades won and the run still lost. Two parameters finished pinned at the low bound of their declared range (risk_per_trade 0.005, take_profit_pct 0.04), so the optimum is OUTSIDE the box and this search has not found it. Widening those bounds is the obvious next search and it must not be justified by the 2026 number. NOT DONE, deliberately: the bear-gate thresholds were not adjusted to make 2026 trade, and the win/loss asymmetry was not re-cut against the forward window. Both would be tuning on the sealed evidence.
statement: A genetic search over 28 declared dimensions, scored by a four-fold walk-forward that rewards consistency rather than magnitude, produces a four-module configuration whose 2026 forward return is better than the hand-set defaults.
